prompts.prompt: PRODUCTION GAME SPRITE SHEET of one existing canonical HOUSE style: grey weathered timber dacha, green entry door, broken mossy slate roof, brick chimney. Attached image is the architectural identity and material reference. Create four actual 90 degree rotations of this SAME building, with consistent dimensions, door and window arrangement, chimney, roof damage and material identity. Exactly FOUR isolated full buildings in a spacious regular 2x2 grid, square canvas, maximum resolution and crisp intricate realistic pixel-art textures. Fixed elevated orthographic isometric camera, looking down about 35 degrees. TOP LEFT: front-left quarter, door facade on left visible face. TOP RIGHT: front-right quarter, same door facade on right visible face, after 90 degree world rotation. BOTTOM LEFT: rear-right quarter, entry hidden behind house, show genuine rear and side architecture. BOTTOM RIGHT: rear-left quarter, entry hidden, genuine back and opposite side. Do not merely mirror frontal facades for back views. Rotate building in world, camera NEVER rotates or changes pitch. Sunlight always from upper-left screen with same lighting direction across all four. No long cast shadows, no ground tiles, no terrain, no text, no grid lines, no people, no additional objects. Rich realistic wood/plaster/roof detail, green-gold clinging ivy restrained close to foundation, warm clear light and natural saturated materials matching reference. Entire isolated building in every quadrant, same scale, at least 15 percent transparent gutter around each, no cells touching or crossing, all four foundation ground pivots centered equally. Truly transparent background with alpha.

PRODUCTION GAME SPRITE ATLAS for ONE canonical abandoned-vehicle asset family and its six approved style variants. Transparent background, portrait 2:3, exactly FOUR COLUMNS and SIX ROWS, 24 isolated sprites, equal regular cells. Reference image establishes realistic rich pixel-art style and the fixed elevated isometric orthographic camera (roughly 35 degrees downward). Every ROW repeats the SAME vehicle at four genuine 90-degree world rotations, seen front-left, front-right, rear-right, rear-left, in that column order. Different rear faces must show rear doors/tailgates and rear lights, NEVER a second front. Keep camera, elevation, vehicle proportions and world lighting fixed. Rows: 1 faded olive Soviet cargo truck with canvas-covered cargo bed; 2 rusty faded BLUE small Soviet van as reference; 3 rusty red old pickup; 4 off-white old compact Soviet sedan with rusty open engine hood; 5 olive old flatbed cargo truck without canvas, wooden bed sides; 6 rusty cream compact sedan with closed hood. Same identity and damage in all four views per row. Warm sunlight always from upper-left screen for ALL views, physically coherent body highlights, believable metal, rubber, cracked windows and small clinging weeds. Readable high-detail realistic pixel game art. Entire vehicle fits its cell, at least 8 percent transparent margin on every side, identical object scale within each row, centered on wheel-contact ground pivot. No people, no buildings, no paved tile or ground islands, no text, no numbers, no UI, no frame dividers, no props between cells, no cast shadow outside vehicle silhouette. Objects upright in the world, NOT arbitrary flat rotation of the same bitmap. Genuine new front/side/back elevations.

PRODUCTION GAME SPRITE ATLAS of ONE existing canonical furniture object: aged wooden kitchen table with four legs, worn plank tabletop, old joints and scratches. Exactly FOUR views in a regular 2 by 2 grid on a transparent square background, generous transparent gutter and entire object visible in every cell. Attached furniture is identity/material reference; transform it into correct elevated ORTHOGRAPHIC ISOMETRIC game art, fixed camera looking down about 35 degrees, same projection as a rural isometric survival game. Top-left view shows front-left quarter; top-right shows front-right quarter after a true 90 degree world rotation; bottom-left shows rear-right quarter after another 90 degrees; bottom-right shows rear-left quarter. All four are the SAME object with unchanged construction and scale seen from different SIDES. Correct visible depth, top surfaces, legs touching the ground plane. Do not simply mirror the same view; the back must be a real back. No flat top-down view, no straight eye-level front view. Exquisite realistic detailed pixel-art treatment, distressed warm brown wood or dark metal, rich nuanced texture and grounded construction, warm light ALWAYS from upper-left screen across all rotations. No people, no room, no floor tile, no extra furniture, no written labels, no numbers, no frames, no extra background objects. Every view centered in its cell with at least 15 percent transparent margin; no overlapping neighboring cells. Keep silhouettes crisp and readable at small game scale.
